The words

In Thy courts let peace be found,
Be Thy temple full of love;
Here we tread on holy ground,
All serene, around, above.

While the knee in prayer is bent,
While with praise the heart o'erflows,
Tranquillize the turbulent!
Give the weary one repose!

Be the place for worship meet,
Meet the worship for the place;
Contemplation's blest retreat,
Shrine of guilelessness and grace!

As an infant knows its home,
Lord! may we Thy temples know;
Hither for instruction come,
Hence by Thee instructed go.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum D and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (F♯), on the word “In”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 14, “The Temple”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: John Bowring (1792–1872)
  • Melody: French Melody, 13th cent.
  • Music (1728): ascr., George Frederick Handel (died undefined)
  • Melody (1850): The Parish Choir, London

Tune INNOCENTS by ascr., George Frederick Handel (died undefined); words by John Bowring (1792–1872).

Sung to the same tune: Day by Day the Manna Fell, God of Mercy, Hear Our Prayer, Hail, All Hail the Joyful Morn, Lord, My Times Are in Thy Hand, Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim, Slowly, by God's Hand Unfurled, Softly Fades the Twilight Ray, Songs of Praise the Angels Sang, They, Who on the Lord Rely, Time by Moments Steals Away, When Before Thy Throne We Kneel.

Questions about In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found

What is the doh of In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found?

In this version, in D major, doh is D. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found start on?

It starts on m (F♯ in D major), a pickup on the word “In” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found in the public domain?

Yes. John Bowring died in 1872, ascr., George Frederick Handel died in undefined; the words were in print by 1848 and the music in 1728. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
